clue.text: Between beginning and end of elections, politician suffers one form of stress

indicators.note: the pieces that follow are placed in the gap between the two letters picked out first
asks for the first and last letters of the word elections

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is the standard crossword politician
to suffer an illness is to have it, so has
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A candidate has a rough time at the polls, from the start of the elections to the count.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying stress on something is giving it special weight or prominence, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Plant with medicinal properties crew introduced to captain

indicators.note: the first piece is put before the second

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan sea captain

explanation.surface: A ship's crew is presented to their skipper.
explanation.definitionFit: This root, a member of the nightshade family, was long used in herbal medicine as a narcotic.

clue.text: Male painting view that incorporates a small flower

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
painting is a form of art

indicators.note: the view's word takes the next pieces inside it

parts.note: to see is to view

explanation.surface: A man's painting of a landscape that includes a little flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old name for the wild pansy, a small flowering plant.

clue.text: Avant-garde artist from English county briefly associated with group of celebs

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Surrey is a county south of London
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: An experimental painter from the Home Counties briefly mixes with famous people.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Surrealist movement, such as Dali and Magritte, were the avant-garde of their day.

clue.text: Surgeon's beginning on break: useless turning up for therapy

indicators.note: take the first letter of the word Surgeon's
in a down answer the letters for useless are read upwards

parts.note: a hiatus is a pause or break
U/S, unserviceable, is a forces abbreviation for useless

explanation.surface: A surgeon starts a holiday by giving up on treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The break's last two letters, the abbreviation for useless, are turned round in place.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Japanese massage therapy applying finger pressure to points on the body.

clue.text: Such stuff in expensive bottles?

indicators.note: here a verb: the words stuff in expensive contain the answer, as a bottle holds wine

explanation.surface: A question about what pricey bottles of wine contain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like a noun for wine bottles; it is the verb, the clue's words holding the answer. The whole clue also describes good wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Costly bottled wine is high-quality stuff, of superior or excellent grade.

clue.text: Herbaceous weed old man cut down at end of garden

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: old man is slang for one's father

indicators.note: take the last letter of garden

explanation.surface: An elderly man cuts back weeds at the bottom of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat hen is a common goosefoot weed, Chenopodium album, found in gardens.

clue.text: Untrustworthy, like a mule?

definitions.meaning: a ... person is evasive and not to be trusted
a mule is a backless shoe, so like one is like a slipper

explanation.surface: A stubborn animal is called unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifty, evasive people are slippery, and a mule shoe resembles a slipper, hence slipper-y.

clue.text: It hard for queen to stomach this dance at end of hippy musical

definitions.text: It hard for queen to stomach this

indicators.note: the dance's word is placed after the musical's

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical about hippies
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A queen struggles to digest something at the closing dance of a 1960s musical.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen here is a female cat, and cats famously cough up balls of fur they cannot digest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat grooming itself swallows fur that clumps in its gut, a mass it cannot digest and must cough up.

clue.text: Regularly turn off broadcast ne at that's showing prejudice

indicators.note: take every other letter of the words turn off, starting from the second

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Someone keeps switching off a programme that seems biased.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'ne at' look like a scanning fragment in the printed text and play no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment that is biased or partial is not just or even-handed, the negative of fair.

clue.text: Buyers of the Times maybe praised her works

indicators.note: the letters of praised her are worked into a new order, as dough is worked

explanation.surface: A newspaper's own puzzle gives its readers a pat on the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of people who buy and read a publication such as this newspaper is its audience.

clue.text: Spoils of war?

parts.note: spoils as a verb means damages or blemishes, while the god of war is the Roman deity of that name

explanation.surface: A question about plunder taken in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To damage or blemish something is to mar it, and the Roman war god's name is spelt the same.

clue.text: Help dunce, one with attitude in

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person, a dunce
the Roman numeral for one is I
a stance is a position or attitude taken on something

explanation.surface: A plea to aid a slow learner who has a bit of an attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing 'in' looks like a scanning fragment and plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Help and aid given to someone are the same thing, so the noun is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Theatre director's talent with comedy pieces over time

indicators.note: the two pieces are turned over and read backwards

parts.note: a farce is a broad comedy
gats are guns, pieces in gangster slang

explanation.surface: A director's gift lies in assembling comic sketches over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' as guns is gangster slang; 'over' reverses the comedy and the guns together, read as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in staging plays, the craft of the theatre, is a director's particular talent.

clue.text: The recommending of a career in advertising

parts.note: ad is short for an advertisement
a vocation is a calling or career

explanation.surface: Someone recommends taking up a job in advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocacy, the act of speaking in favour of something, is recommending it.

clue.text: Setter for example rejected language of old

indicators.note: turned back, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: Latin is the classical language of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, for instance, turns down a dead language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the puzzle compiler; here it is a substance that makes a liquid set.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelling agent makes jellies and desserts set firm, so it is a setter in the literal sense.

clue.text: With a nasty turn during illness, I'm looking for some fun

indicators.note: the following letters go inside the illness

parts.note: gout is a painful disease of the joints

indicators.note: the word for nasty is turned back to front

parts.note: bad means nasty

explanation.surface: Someone is suffering a nasty turn during an illness, but still wants to enjoy themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm looking for some fun' is the gadabout speaking: the definition is a person, though phrased as a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasure-seeker who flits from one amusement to another is a restless seeker of fun.

clue.text: Extremely attached to one sort of transport cafe

indicators.note: the second word is joined on after the first

parts.note: a car is one kind of transport
very means extremely

explanation.surface: Someone is very fond of a roadside transport cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: An eatery serving carved roast meats is a kind of restaurant or cafe.

clue.text: During journey, Old Bill's seen parked … here?

indicators.note: the following letters go inside the journey

parts.note: a ride is a journey
a bill is an advertisement, an ad, so bills are ads

explanation.surface: On a trip, someone notices a police car pulled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' looks like the police; it splits into O for old and ADS, bill as poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Cars, including police cars, are often left parked at the verge beside a road.

clue.text: More dainty New York restaurant accommodating most of family

indicators.note: the restaurant holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a diner is the classic American roadside restaurant

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

parts.note: kin are family

explanation.surface: A New York eatery serves most of a family that is more elegant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinky is British informal for neat and dainty, so the comparative is more dainty.

clue.text: Ruling body's terrible anger about mini October revolution

indicators.note: the joined words go around the next piece

parts.note: dire means dreadful or terrible
ire is anger

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the short month's letters are rearranged

parts.note: Oct is the short form of the month October

explanation.surface: A government faces terrible anger over a small revolt in October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' is the anagram signal on the short month; the Directory ruled France from 1795 after the Revolution, so the October uprising fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Directory was the five-man executive that governed revolutionary France in the 1790s.

clue.text: I was brought in to manage Anglican Church

definitions.text: I was brought in to manage Anglican Church

parts.note: to run something is to manage it

indicators.note: the letter I goes inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A new head speaks of being appointed to run the Church of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Runcie was Archbishop of Canterbury, head of the Church of England, 1980-91.
explanation.definitionFit: As Archbishop of Canterbury this prelate was appointed to lead the Church of England.

clue.text: Home help's plan to finish early er

indicators.note: the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a chart is a plan or map

explanation.surface: A domestic cleaner's scheme is to knock off early.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing 'er' looks like a scanning fragment and plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman or charlady is a British cleaner employed in a private home.

clue.text: Old car somebody has crashed in into kerb, unfortunately

indicators.note: the crashed letters go inside the other piece
an unfortunate result rearranges the letters of kerb

parts.note: one means a person, somebody

indicators.note: the letters of the person and has are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Somebody has driven an old car into the kerb.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagram signals: 'crashed' on the person and has, 'unfortunately' on kerb, which then wraps around the first. The stray 'in' looks like a scanning fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: An old rattling vehicle, originally an early bicycle, shakes its riders' bones.

clue.text: Put up with persistent cough

definitions.meaning: to be able to cope with or tolerate something, as in can't stand it

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a cough that will not go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally to cope with or tolerate, and a dry repeated cough is also a hacking one.

clue.text: Woman heading out of Spanish region

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

parts.note: Galicia is a region in north-west Spain

explanation.surface: A woman sets off from a region of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Circus performer's accessory pawnbroker has kept reserved

indicators.note: the pawnbroker holds the next piece inside

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker
icy can mean cold and reserved in manner

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker is holding on to a circus artist's prop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' as slang for a pawnbroker is old British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-wheeled cycle is a prop ridden by circus performers.

clue.text: On one day of the week stays in and trains

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter's heading

indicators.note: the day's letters hold the word in inside them

parts.note: Tues is short for Tuesday

explanation.surface: Someone stays indoors on one particular weekday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trains' is a noun here: a train is a group of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A train of attendants following a dignitary is a retinue, so the plurals match.
